fired-clay-figurines-venus.research_focus: the fired-clay figurines of Dolni Vestonice in Moravia, about 27,000 years ago, and the hearth they were baked in
fired-clay-figurines-venus.scene: Ice Age hunter-gatherers in furs crouch around a stone-ringed hearth, one lifting a small fired-clay female figurine from the embers; a mammoth-bone hut stands behind

lime-plaster-burning.research_focus: early lime burning in the Near East, limestone heated in pit kilns and slaked into plaster for floors and walls
lime-plaster-burning.scene: Early villagers tend a smouldering pit of burning limestone beside a mud-walled house; a woman smooths pale wet plaster across the floor with a flat stone

first-copper-smelting-balkans.research_focus: Belovode in Serbia, about 5000 BC: green copper ore, charcoal, small pit furnaces and clay crucibles
first-copper-smelting-balkans.scene: Neolithic smelters crouch over a small clay-lined furnace, blowing through a clay pipe to raise the fire as a bright trickle of molten copper runs from green ore into a crucible

varna-gold-grave-treasure.research_focus: the Varna Necropolis on the Black Sea coast, with its gold beads, rings and plaques laid in graves
varna-gold-grave-treasure.scene: A burial pit on a Black Sea hillside where mourners lay a body on its back, its chest and hands covered in glittering hammered gold ornaments, the sea beyond

mesopotamian-kiln-fired-bricks.research_focus: fired brick making in southern Mesopotamia: moulded mud bricks, domed kilns and brick walls beside the rivers
mesopotamian-kiln-fired-bricks.scene: Workers on a river plain stack moulded mud bricks into a domed kiln with flames at its base, while others carry baked red bricks toward a rising wall

bronze-alloyed-sumer.research_focus: bronze casting in Sumer: ingots of copper and tin, crucibles, stone moulds and early bronze tools
bronze-alloyed-sumer.scene: A Sumerian smith in a kilted skirt tips a glowing crucible of molten metal into a stone mould, with ingots of copper and tin laid out beside the furnace

glass-made-mesopotamia.research_focus: early Mesopotamian glassmaking: furnaces, sand and ash, core-formed vessels and beads
glass-made-mesopotamia.scene: Craftsmen at a brick furnace wind a thread of glowing glass around a clay core to shape a small flask, with bowls of sand and ash beside them and finished glass beads on a mat

mesoamerican-rubber-curing.research_focus: Gulf coast rubber working, milky latex from rubber trees mixed with morning glory juice, and rubber balls
mesoamerican-rubber-curing.scene: Gulf-coast villagers beside a tapped rubber tree stir white latex with crushed vine juice in a clay bowl, while a child bounces a dark rubber ball on packed earth

hittite-iron-mastery.research_focus: Bronze Age Anatolian ironworking: bloomery furnaces, hammered blooms, and iron blades and tools
hittite-iron-mastery.scene: An Anatolian smith in a stone-walled forge hammers a glowing lump of iron on an anvil, with a row of dark iron blades and tools cooling on a rack behind

roman-concrete-perfected.research_focus: Roman concrete: volcanic pozzolana ash, lime and rubble packed into timber forms, as in harbour piers and domes
roman-concrete-perfected.scene: Roman builders in tunics shovel volcanic ash and lime into a wooden form beside a harbour, ramming in rubble while a half-built round vault rises behind them

glassblowing-invented-syria.research_focus: early glassblowing in the Levant in the first century BC: blowpipes, small furnaces and thin blown vessels
glassblowing-invented-syria.scene: A craftsman in a Levantine workshop puffs his cheeks as he blows down a long iron pipe, inflating a glowing bubble of glass, with finished small flasks lined up on a shelf

tang-true-porcelain.research_focus: Tang dynasty kilns in China: white kaolin clay, high-fired kilns, thin white translucent wares
tang-true-porcelain.scene: Tang-era potters in a hillside dragon kiln village open a firing chamber to lift out a gleaming, thin white bowl, with rows of unfired cups drying on boards behind

murano-cristallo-glass.research_focus: Venetian cristallo at Murano in the fifteenth century: clear glass goblets, furnaces and the island workshops
murano-cristallo-glass.scene: A master glassmaker in a Renaissance Venetian furnace room turns a glowing gather on a pipe to form a clear goblet, while finished colourless glass vessels catch the light on a table

bottger-european-porcelain.research_focus: early European hard-paste porcelain at Dresden and Meissen: laboratory furnaces and white porcelain pieces
bottger-european-porcelain.scene: An eighteenth-century alchemist in a powdered wig and long coat lifts a small white porcelain cup from a brick kiln in a cramped laboratory lined with crucibles and jars

darby-coke-smelting.research_focus: Coalbrookdale in Shropshire in 1709: a charcoal-style blast furnace fed with coke, with bellows and a waterwheel
darby-coke-smelting.scene: Ironworkers in a stone blast-furnace yard barrow black coke up a ramp to the furnace mouth, a water wheel turning beside it, as molten iron runs into sand moulds below

parkesine-first-plastic.research_focus: Alexander Parkes's Parkesine at the 1862 International Exhibition in London: moulded cellulose combs, boxes and medallions
parkesine-first-plastic.scene: A Victorian exhibition stand in a glass hall, its table covered with small carved and moulded dark combs, boxes and buttons, a gentleman in a frock coat holding one up to a crowd

polyethylene-discovered-icl.research_focus: the 1933 high-pressure experiments at Winnington in Cheshire: a heavy steel reaction vessel and the waxy white solid found inside
polyethylene-discovered-icl.scene: A 1930s laboratory where a technician in a white coat peers into a heavy steel pressure vessel on a bench, a small waxy white lump in his tongs, gauges and thick pipes behind

synthetic-diamonds-ge.research_focus: the 1954 General Electric high-pressure press at Schenectady and its small synthetic diamonds
synthetic-diamonds-ge.scene: A 1950s laboratory with a huge iron hydraulic press, its steel anvils opened to show a small graphite cylinder and a few tiny glittering diamonds on a tray; no people

pilkington-float-glass.research_focus: the float glass process at Pilkington in St Helens: a ribbon of molten glass drawn across a bath of molten tin
pilkington-float-glass.scene: A long factory hall in the 1950s where a glowing ribbon of molten glass slides out across a bath of shining tin, flat and level, as workers in aprons watch from a walkway
